name: Soy-Baked Salmon Rice Bowl with Mango Cabbage Slaw & Cilantro

instructions.primary_message: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
While the water is heating, place soy sauce, oil, honey, and spices in a baking dish. Whisk to combine the marinade.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 tsp toasted sesame oil
honey
1 tsp garlic powder
black pepper
salt

instructions.primary_message: Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, if using salmon with skin, place the fillet, skin-side down, on a cutting board. Holding the tail end (or corner) firmly, use a knife to cut between the flesh and skin; continue to cut through the length of the fillet (take care not to cut through the skin); discard the skin.
Cut the salmon into 1-inch cubes. Add to the baking dish with the marinade, stir to coat, and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 small bunch cilantro
1 lime
1 medium head napa cabbage
1 mango

instructions.primary_message: Using a clean cutting board, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half in a medium bowl. (Reserve remaining cilantro for serving.)
Juice lime into the bowl with the cilantro. Add mayo, soy sauce, honey, and spices, then whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ cup mayonnaise
honey
salt
black pepper
¼ tsp crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: Trim off and discard root end of cabbage; halve lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides; medium dice. Add to the bowl.
Peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl, stir combine the slaw, and set aside.
When the rice has about 10 minutes left, place salmon in the oven and bake, flipping once, until golden and cooked through, 8-10 minutes. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide rice, salmon, and slaw between bowls. Top with reserved cilantro and enjoy!
